title: The White Lab Coat
content:
Detective Laura Mendes arrived at a small research laboratory just after eight in the morning. Something valuable had disappeared during the night, and the police believed that someone inside the building was responsible.

The missing object was a small box containing several experimental samples. It had been kept in a locked laboratory.

Laura walked around the room carefully. There were no broken windows, and the door had been locked when the security guard arrived.

— Who was working here last night? — she asked.

— Only three people had access to the laboratory — the manager replied. — Dr. Martin, Julia, and Thomas.

Laura looked at the desks. Everything seemed normal until she noticed something hanging behind the door.

It was a white lab coat.

— Whose coat is this?

— I'm not sure. Everyone has one.

Laura examined it carefully. There was a small blue mark on one of the sleeves.

— Did anyone notice anything unusual last night?

Julia raised her hand.

— I saw Thomas leaving the laboratory around ten o'clock.

Thomas immediately looked nervous.

— I was only going home. I didn't take anything.

Laura didn't accuse him. Instead, she continued investigating.

She checked the security cameras. The recording showed Thomas leaving the building at ten, but there was no recording of him entering the laboratory after that.

Then Laura examined the lab coat again.

Inside one of its pockets, she found a small access card.

— This card belongs to Dr. Martin, doesn't it?

The manager looked surprised.

— Yes. But Dr. Martin told me that he had lost it yesterday.

Laura looked at the three employees.

— Then we have an interesting problem.

She checked the access records. The card had been used at 9:45 p.m., less than fifteen minutes before Thomas left the building.

— Thomas, did you use Dr. Martin's card?

— No. I didn't even know he had lost it.

Laura then noticed something else. The blue mark on the lab coat matched the blue ink used in a special printer inside the laboratory.

She checked the printer and found a small piece of paper under it.

It contained a list of the missing samples.

— Who printed this list? — Laura asked.

Nobody answered.

Finally, Dr. Martin looked down.

— I did.

Laura turned toward him.

— Why?

He explained that he had discovered that someone was planning to steal the samples. He had secretly printed a list to identify which samples were missing.

Laura thought for a moment.

— Then why was your access card inside the lab coat?

Dr. Martin became silent.

The detective checked the coat one more time. The name tag had been removed, but a small thread was still attached to it.

She compared it with the uniforms worn by the three employees.

The thread matched Dr. Martin's coat.

— You weren't investigating the theft, were you? You were trying to make it look as if someone else had stolen the samples.

Dr. Martin finally admitted the truth. He had taken the samples himself and planned to sell them to a private company.

The lab coat had seemed like an insignificant detail, but it had revealed the connection between the access card, the printer, and the stolen samples.

Laura smiled as the police arrived.

— Sometimes the smallest piece of evidence can tell the biggest story.
